channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot
item.description: Gemini 4 Neon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot for agentic coding, multistep tool use and knowledge work, with Google claiming quality close to Gemini 4 Carbon at a lower token cost per task, faster responses and fewer unrequested changes. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency
item.description: DaisyRose-27B, RadixArk's first model built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with Miles, lifts Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 from 5.6% to 12.0% with 1,200 curated tasks over 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs, cutting training cost 57%. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon
item.description: Google's Gemini 4 Neon offers frontier-level intelligence for complex coding and analysis at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1-million-token context window and a 70.9% Vals Index score ranking second. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: The Gemini app is now available on lower-memory Android devices.
item.description: Google's Gemini app now runs on lower-memory Android Go edition devices, bringing Gemini Live conversations in more than 45 languages and Nano Banana image generation to those phones. (Google AI Blog)

item.title: Inside the Codex sandbox
item.description: Codex’s :workspace permission profile writes to the workspace by default while making .git and .codex read-only and disabling network access, with OpenAI detailing how macOS, Linux and Windows enforce those limits. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Why your fine-tuning job takes longer than the FLOPs say
item.description: Across 272 production SFT runs, FLOP-based estimates reached only R²=0.31 and 12.41 h MAE, while CatBoost using pre-scheduling information hit R²=0.98 and 1.71 h MAE, explaining why fine-tuning often outruns FLOP predictions. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Connect Supabase, Box, Calendly, and more to Copilot
item.description: GitHub added eight GitHub-verified MCP connectors to Copilot in public preview, letting users ask why a Buildkite build failed and fix the code in the same session or check a Supabase schema before writing a migration. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Genie 4 is now available
item.description: Google AI Ultra subscribers can now use Genie 4 to generate interactive worlds with real-time audio and editing, including natural-language weather changes, added characters and a community gallery. (Google DeepMind)

item.title: How Sumitomo Life’s leaders helped teams adopt ChatGPT Enterprise
item.description: Sumitomo Life, after a 100–150-person ChatGPT Business pilot starting in 2023, upgraded to ChatGPT Enterprise in June 2026, with executives and the president modeling use and employee-reported time savings supporting an estimated 203% ROI. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Wait for pull request events with GitHub CLI
item.description: GitHub CLI v2.105.0 adds GitHub Event Streams so `gh event listen` can wait on a pull request URL for events such as a submitted review, emitting JSON lines instead of polling in a loop. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Time-Series Models in the Streamhouse: A New Frontier and Use Cases
item.description: IBM's time-series foundation models, with more than 50 million downloads, are now natively integrated into Confluent for cloud and on-premises deployment on CPUs, using Apache Flink SQL to forecast and detect anomalies in streaming data. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: AI edits circuits itself: OpenAI has models optimize chips, improving AMD flagship GPU performance-per-watt by up to 14%
item.description: GPT-4o rewrote Jalapeño circuits, cutting a new multiplier's area by about 15% and latency to one clock cycle, while SystemVerilog RTL edits on AMD's flagship GPU lifted PPA up to 14%, compressing a year of optimization into under five months. (AIbase)

item.title: The Silent Consensus
item.description: After frontier AI discovered vulnerabilities in internet core infrastructure during “Black October,” the “silent consensus” argument holds that once AI can conduct R&D, negotiate, allocate capital and manufacture, markets may force humans to cede dominance over global commerce. (OpenAI News)

item.title: AI assistant competition shifts to work context management: Tencent WorkBuddy rethinks task organization with groups and multi-folder linking
item.description: Starting November 19, Tencent WorkBuddy's desktop 5.11.3 update renames Tasks to Recent, upgrades Spaces to Groups, and reorganizes the sidebar by work items, adding drag-and-drop grouping, pinning and multi-folder association. (AIbase)

item.title: Customize GitHub Copilot for your team
item.description: GitHub Copilot team customizations are generally available for organization teams, letting maintainers set approved Agent Plugins as defaults for direct members in VS Code, the Copilot app and Copilot CLI for Copilot Business and Enterprise with no sub-team inheritance. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Research acceleration: The jagged frontier
item.description: Internal measurements from OpenAI show coding agents accelerating and reshaping the AI development cycle, with new quantitative and qualitative indicators of AI uplift across research areas and human involvement, and a call to publicly report RSI metrics. (OpenAI News)

item.title: AI compute drives up memory costs as Apple looks to sign four-year DRAM deal with Samsung
item.description: A November 18 report says Apple plans a rare four- to five-year DRAM supply agreement with Samsung Electronics, locking in minimum purchase volumes from the first half of 2027 through 2031 or 2032, as surging AI computing demand tightens chip supply. (AIbase)

item.title: Security risk assessments run automatically on GitHub Team
item.description: GitHub Team organizations now run free security risk assessments automatically, letting admins and security managers review findings on exposed credentials and code vulnerabilities to understand current risk and prioritize next steps. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Managing frontier AI risk: From training to deployment
item.description: OpenAI describes a four-layer defense-in-depth approach spanning research, internal deployment and external deployment, and says it has paused internal training or delayed the release of GPT-6.1 Astra to pace frontier-model risk. (OpenAI News)

item.title: Anthropic discloses post-IPO equity details, with Amazon and Google holding a combined stake of nearly 30%
item.description: On November 17, Anthropic disclosed that Amazon holds 14.7% and Google 13.7% post-IPO, nearly 30% combined, with Amazon reaching up to 23.8% if all convertible notes convert and committing over $100 billion in AWS spending over ten years. (AIbase)
